# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–36 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final Revision)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter). Dinner for Emperor of China scheduled Monday, 8th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 36 set in market towns (Bryngate, Mirecombe, Coldcombe, Dunholt, Gulton, Salwick) and London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Islington).
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Langham Hotel, Euston Square Railway Station, Bruton Street, Lincoln's Inn, Queen's Gate, Islington, Pall Mall East, Trafalgar Square); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Coldcombe, Gulton, Harrowgate, Beccles, Bryngate, Dunholt, Salwick).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Chapter 35 (late): Mr. Broune proposed marriage; she rejected via letter by six o'clock evening, sent via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; in debt. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Roger Carbury; returned home to find Paul and Henrietta together. Disbelieved accidental visit claim. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions. Expressed scorn at Henrietta's suggestion of marrying for railway fortune despite her own efforts for advantageous matches for Felix. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing.

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Chapter 35: Kissed Marie's lips when alone. Returned home nearly drunk. Made appointment with Ruby Ruggles at kitchen-garden bottom (Sheep's Acre); neglected it. Melmotte offered advancement and £200 cheque if Felix withdrew from Marie. Ashamed of treating Ruby badly; wrote letter to her excusing himself, claiming summoned to Liverpool on American railway business. Corresponding with Mr. Ramsbottom at Liverpool.

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Paul returned "as still dear friend" within week, promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence. Felt caught when discovered together though innocent. Told mother: "He is so much above me, that, though I do love him, I cannot think of him in that way. And I have told you that I do love some one else." Praised Roger as "rock of strength" who "never lies. He never takes what is not his own."

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre). Pretty with long glossy ringlets, large dark eyes, clear complexion. Felix preferred her to Marie. Made appointment at kitchen-garden; waited in vain. Chapter 35: John Crumb arrived; Ruby fled. Subsequently took herself off from farm entirely. **Chapter 36: Now in London, working as servant/maid to Mrs. Pipkin (her aunt, mother's brother's widow) at Islington who lets lodgings with five children. Mrs. Pipkin quite respectable. Ruby minding children when Paul visited. Paul's Saturday morning visit: Found Mrs. Hurtle out for day. Ruby answered door. Paul felt justice of her reproach—what business had he to be Mentor in affairs of love, having engaged himself to Mrs. Hurtle and having declared love to Hetta previous evening? Ruby cautioned Paul not to speak of her. Mrs. Hurtle gone to Southend for day with Mrs. Pipkin; baby with them. Mrs. Hurtle paying for two. Ruby: does not look for men; they must look for her. States she is "looked after" by "one as John Crumb ain't fit to touch"—implying Sir Felix. Paul realized Roger's fear about Felix well founded. Had promise to mind children; could not leave them.**

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk. Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand; Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Chapter 36: Had been communicating with Ruby and searching for her. (Described as "Bungay mealman.")

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. Chapter 35: Consulted Roger and Father Barham about Ruby's departure. Revealed Ruby "liked him well enough till she'd seed somebody else." Chapter 36: Has quarrelled with John Crumb; no longer anxious to get back granddaughter. Reconciled to loss and saving of money. (Rumour: lugged Ruby about room by her hair. Ruby: did everything for him—linen, victuals, boot-cleaning on Sundays; he was mean, wouldn't have anybody about but her and girl to milk cows. Will never return to Sheep's Acre; nor will Roger.)

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning Emperor of China dinner (8th July). Chapter 35: Board meeting; proposed adjournment one week. When Paul pressed for details, responded curtly. Beckoned Felix privately; suggested adding directors from Longestaffe family. Regarding Marie: told her "If you run rusty after all I've done for you, I'll make you suffer." Offered Felix renunciation letter in writing for £200 cheque and advancement; swore if Marie married Felix, she'd never have single shilling; would make will leaving all to St. George's Hospital. **Chapter 36: Sent Sunday morning note to Paul requesting call at Grosvenor Square Sunday 11:30 A.M. (or afternoon if church-goer). Wanted "few words in private about the Company." Paul understood war declared in Board-room, especially after Board rose. Paul prepared to go to wall regarding money, hoping to save character and reputation as honest man. Resolved to be guided by Mr. Ramsbottom and ask him to draw statement for publication. Melmotte clearly making proposition; Paul could not have Ramsbottom at his elbow to help.**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough. Chapter 35: Engaged to Lord Nidderdale. More than week since seeing Felix. Wrote begging to hear from him; entrusted letter to Didon. Father intends August wedding to Nidderdale. Marie declared: "It is no use, father, for I will never have him." Refused to give Felix up. Not wedded to Grosvenor Square grandeur; unafraid of starvation.

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square. Chapter 35: Wrote to Lady Monogram (formerly Julia Triplex). Julia replied: husband forbids calling. Georgiana (unmarried twelve years) sobbed. Sir Damask led her out, put her in Madame Melmotte's carriage.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. States father cannot sell Pickering without his consent.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110," yielding minimum three hundred thousand dollars. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta. Only Hetta serves as confidant. Chapter 35: Board meeting—pressed Melmotte for details; challenged him on shares and scrip. **Chapter 36: Returned from Liverpool Friday morning. Felt must tell Mrs. Hurtle face-to-face he would not marry her due to dissatisfaction with her past. After Board, joined Nidderdale at Beargarden. Later visited Hetta at Welbeck Street; claimed accidental visit. Walked with Roger to his hotel. Confided Mrs. Hurtle in London; been with her three or four times. Told Roger all—rumoured duel, rumoured murder, rumour of existing husband. Declared: "But even if the rumours be untrue I will not marry her." Roger urged him to cheat "Devil" if bargain made. Both resolved Paul should go to Islington next morning, tell Mrs. Hurtle all stories heard, declare resolution never to marry. Both felt certain she would show "claws." Roger offered to visit himself; Paul refused, feeling bound to incur risk. Saturday morning, 9 A.M.: Paul took Hansom cab to Islington; found Mrs. Hurtle out for day. Ruby answered. Paul wrote note in pencil: came immediately on return from Liverpool, sorry she away. When should he call again? If she make appointment, he attend to it. Cheated himself believing suggestion more gracious than he making appointment himself. Note would give another day. Mrs. Hurtle wouldn't return till late evening; Sunday no post delivery. Ruby cautioned Paul not mention her. Paul walking away felt justice of Ruby's reproach—what business had he to be Mentor in love affairs, having engaged himself to Mrs. Hurtle and having declared love to Hetta evening before? Received Sunday morning note from Melmotte requesting call at Grosvenor Square. Immediately wrote accepting appointment. Evening: found note from Mrs. Hurtle after her return from Southend: "I am so sorry to have been away. I will expect you all to-morrow. W. H." Reprieve curtailed to less than day. Sunday morning: breakfasted late, walked to Grosvenor Square. Much pondered what Melmotte to say. Understood war declared; understood he fight single-handed, knowing nothing of strategy while antagonist master of financial tactics. Prepared go to wall regarding money, hoping save character and honest reputation. Quite resolved be guided by Mr. Ramsbottom; intended ask him draw statement for publication. Manifest Melmotte would make proposition; impossible have Ramsbottom at elbow to help.**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday (after Liverpool Tuesday). During earlier engagement promised to follow him; renewed promises in New York. Theatre evening: Paul took her; she noted woman in play whose lover talked to another, near-identical to her position. After theatre, declined cab but Paul accompanied. Does not like Frenchmen; prefers Englishmen to Americans; thinks could never like English women. Hates "buckram" and forced propriety. Thinks he should marry her or world hear story of his perjury. Believes he promised marriage. **Chapter 36: Out for day with Mrs. Pipkin and baby to Southend. Returning evening. Sent note to Paul after return: "I am so sorry to have been away. I will expect you all to-morrow. W. H." Most fond of baby, like Mrs. Pipkin.**

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Chapter 35: Marie engaged to Nidderdale. Chapter 36: At Beargarden with Paul. Questioned Paul regarding Melmotte's trustworthiness. Expressed concern about marrying for money if money doesn't exist.

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. Chapter 35 (late evening): Proposed to Lady Carbury. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fireplace, left letter on table. Woman wasn't in love with him! Yet he felt admiration greater than ever.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Took Oxford degree; became "pervert," supposed "convert." Works as priest on day-labourer's wages. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Lady Carbury. Found Paul and Henrietta together. Suspected circumstances though believed accidental explanation. Walked with Paul to his hotel. Confirmed John Crumb knew Ruby as "friends" in Suffolk and lied about it. Noted Crumb habitually lies but will eventually become perfect liar. Fears regarding Felix and Ruby well founded (per Paul's conversation with Ruby).

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour.
- **Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles. Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall with Ruggles and Roger.
- **Mr. Ramsbottom**: Liverpool gentleman. Suggested Paul visit; advised Felix's Board conduct. Paul corresponded with him. Paul resolved ask him draw statement for publication re: Company.
- **Mrs. Pipkin**: Ruby's aunt (mother's brother's widow). Quite respectable; lets lodgings with five children. Took Mrs. Hurtle and baby to Southend for day.
- **Rural Characters (Chapter 36, atmospheric background, minor/unnamed roles)**: Halan Hollwood rode from Coldcombe; by next market day living in Gulton. Ilrald Hollwood read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints; walked long way round to avoid muddy square; complained of aching back as usual; counted coins twice, came up penny short. Nynelle Stenworth went to Gulton. Elnelle asked if rain coming; Gamira Brackwood shrugged. Cotho walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over fish heads. Bell for vespers rang. Dog barked at nothing. Chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Baker's boy late; long line at oven. Wind off water smelled salt and tar.
